title: Optimal stretch for online bin stretching
formal: Determine the smallest worst-case stretch of deterministic online packing into \(m\) bins when the full sequence is promised to fit offline into \(m\) unit-capacity bins, in the regime of arbitrarily large \(m\).
definitions: Definitions and model details remain incomplete. Specify whether the target is a supremum or a limiting value over \(m\), item range and additive conventions; the former three-halves threshold is already surpassed.
answer_criterion: Supply a real approximation to the defined optimal constant and a Lean-checked proof of absolute error at most \(1/100\). Exact determination also qualifies; the approximation does not establish an associated exact conjecture. This is a provisional candidate, not a completed benchmark specification. Pending: Specify whether the target is a supremum or a limiting value over \(m\), item range and additive conventions; the former three-halves threshold is already surpassed.
context: The supplied catalogue associates this question with Jirí Sgall. This is an editorial research connection, not a claim of authorship or a personal research agenda. The candidate retains the bibliography and dated caveats from that catalogue; these have not received a comprehensive independent literature review.
why: This measures how much extra capacity is needed when the number of bins is fixed but item order is online.

import_provenance.original_title: The optimal stretch for online bin stretching
import_provenance.original_statement: Determine the smallest worst-case stretch achievable by deterministic online packing into m bins when the entire item sequence is promised to fit offline in m unit bins. Items must be assigned irrevocably, and the central target is the optimal ratio for arbitrarily large m.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The 3/2 barrier was already broken before the cutoff: the cited paper gives 139/93<1.495 for sufficiently large m. The remaining question is the optimal ratio.
